candidates.name: The Shade Stitcher
candidates.silhouette: Tall human, narrow apron, triangular bundle of shade battens rising over one shoulder.
candidates.setup: Paid to keep the market's shade intact; another torn panel costs her the afternoon's earnings.
candidates.quirk: Holds spare pegs between her lips and tests every knot with a hard tug.
candidates.role: Her routine lowering and raising of a cloth panel gives Harper a visible escape opportunity to plan for.
candidates.biologicalDirection: Paired opposable thumb tips let the stitcher tension cord and manipulate pegs with unusually secure precision.

candidates.name: The Water Porter
candidates.silhouette: Short, ochre-skinned humanoid beneath a wide yoke of squat ceramic jars.
candidates.setup: Responsible for delivering a full measure; every lost drop comes out of his pay.
candidates.quirk: Stops to settle the water before making a tight turn.
candidates.role: Creates a slow moving bottleneck that the children can time and a pursuing guard must negotiate without wrecking valuable stock.

candidates.name: The Scrap Appraiser
candidates.silhouette: Small older human, tiered pockets, one oversized folding magnifier.
candidates.setup: Buys useful salvage cheaply and fears paying for a worthless part.
candidates.quirk: Weighs a piece in one palm before ever looking at its seller.
candidates.role: Takes an interest in what Taffy is carrying; the boy has to conceal the newly stolen device while appearing ordinary.
candidates.biologicalDirection: An enlarged precision eye and tactile fingertip pads suggest an inherited or engineered ability to inspect and judge salvaged parts.

candidates.name: The Screen Keeper
candidates.silhouette: Lanky humanoid carrying a flat triangular ladder and a rolled cleaning pad.
candidates.setup: Maintains public information displays and needs traders to keep subscribing.
candidates.quirk: Polishes one particular corner even while reading the screen.
candidates.role: Gives the opening information display a human presence; the pair can observe its update cycle while looking like casual passersby.

candidates.name: The Flask Redeemer
candidates.silhouette: Broad human in a low sun hat, pushing a tiny cart piled above their own head.
candidates.setup: Collects returnable containers and remembers precisely who owes a deposit.
candidates.quirk: Rattles each flask beside an ear to check that it is empty.
candidates.role: A noisy, awkward crossing can conceal a brief movement, but brushing the cart risks attracting everyone's attention.

candidates.name: The Quiet Stallholder
candidates.silhouette: Long-fingered offworld human behind a shallow stall with folding wooden wings.
candidates.setup: Needs enough sales to pay tomorrow's rent; dislikes the water broker's cut.
candidates.quirk: Keeps straightening a single item customers never buy.
candidates.role: Notices the children arrive together, then separately; can choose to continue a sale rather than inform the broker. A small decision with moral weight.
candidates.biologicalDirection: Two pairs of hands and wider peripheral vision let this quietly observant trader sort stock while monitoring the street.

candidates.name: Doorpost
candidates.silhouette: Broad wedge-shaped humanoid, heavy work coat, one shoulder padded for moving crates.
candidates.setup: Paid to keep people away from the boss and treats personal space as a strict boundary.
candidates.quirk: Turns his whole body instead of just his head.
candidates.role: His turns open and close the line of sight to Taffy. He can become the visible pursuer Harper draws into the public passage.

candidates.name: The Tester
candidates.silhouette: Very thin human in a faded but meticulously kept apron, ceramic inspection lens on a cord.
candidates.setup: Values jewels for the broker and needs to remain the person who cannot be fooled.
candidates.quirk: Always tries to take an object out of its owner's hand to examine it properly.
candidates.role: Raises the stakes of Harper's performance by trying to inspect the fake gem. She has to keep control while directing his and the broker's gaze.

candidates.name: Tally
candidates.silhouette: Compact older humanoid, rectangular ledger boards folded against the chest.
candidates.setup: Keeps the broker's accounts and expects to be blamed for missing property.
candidates.quirk: Counts tools and cups as reflexively as money.
candidates.role: Can notice the empty key holster after the children leave and initiate the alert. Gives the wanted broadcast a possible causal origin.

candidates.name: Fast Coat
candidates.silhouette: Long-legged humanoid in a sleeveless coat with two blunt hanging tails.
candidates.setup: A junior enforcer hoping that a conspicuous success will earn a better position.
candidates.quirk: Signals bystanders out of his way as if he already commands them.
candidates.role: A fast, committed pursuer makes Harper's decoy route dangerous; she needs concealment and a planned turn to lose him.
candidates.biologicalDirection: A compact muscular balancing tail helps the enforcer change direction quickly while pursuing people through tight lanes.

candidates.name: Stillwater
candidates.silhouette: Ordinary-looking human in an unremarkable plain wrap, small still movements.
candidates.setup: Earns a living spotting accomplices while louder colleagues confront the obvious distraction.
candidates.quirk: Watches hands and reflections rather than faces.
candidates.role: Makes the hidden partnership the central risk. The boy needs a real broken sightline; this watcher is difficult to draw toward the gem.
candidates.biologicalDirection: Wraparound eyes make the watcher's attention difficult to read while they monitor hands and reflections.

candidates.name: Valve Hand
candidates.silhouette: Squat humanoid, oversized padded gloves, short apron marked by mineral deposits.
candidates.setup: Maintains the broker's pumps; a damaged valve is his problem even when the boss causes it.
candidates.quirk: Moves other people's cups off machinery without asking.
candidates.role: Can interrupt the jewel exchange to reach a control beside the chair, briefly threatening Taffy's cover without having noticed him.
candidates.biologicalDirection: Dense organic contact skin and flexible mineral-like hand plates suit repeated work on hot, abrasive pump hardware.

candidates.name: The Pipe Fitter
candidates.silhouette: Human with one long protective glove, a shoulder roll of tools and a low work stool.
candidates.setup: Must finish a pressure adjustment before the supply cycle changes.
candidates.quirk: Answers everything with their eyes still on the pressure needle.
candidates.role: A valve release masks a few footsteps, while the fitter's work position closes one route. The children must read and time that routine.
candidates.biologicalDirection: Small protected breathing valves and a throat reserve suggest a lineage adapted to confined, humid pipework and brief breath-holding.

candidates.name: The Cloth Carrier
candidates.silhouette: A walking rectangular frame draped with several uneven lengths of repaired awning.
candidates.setup: Returning shade panels to their owners and unwilling to deliver dusty work twice.
candidates.quirk: Snaps each bottom corner straight before folding.
candidates.role: A moving cloth screen gives Harper a moment to vanish. Strong alternative to using the market stitcher's panel.

candidates.name: The Route Runner
candidates.silhouette: Lean older teenager, cropped work jacket, one long dispatch tube strapped horizontally.
candidates.setup: A late delivery threatens their wages; the service ledge is their usual shortcut.
candidates.quirk: Changes the tube from side to side at every narrow opening without stopping.
candidates.role: Meets Taffy coming the other way and forces him into a pump recess. That brief interruption can hide him from the street or expose the sack.

candidates.name: The Pressure Warden
candidates.silhouette: Broad human in a stiff sun cape, carrying a flat inspection board.
candidates.setup: Responsible for keeping the public out of working water infrastructure.
candidates.quirk: Checks a latch twice, even after seeing it catch.
candidates.role: Closes the obvious maintenance gate on schedule, forcing a choice of path. Needs an early glimpse of the routine so the obstacle feels earned.
candidates.biologicalDirection: Broad contact pads and recessed ear membranes suggest sensitivity to mechanical vibration and pressure changes in gates and pipes.

candidates.name: The Late Lunch
candidates.silhouette: Heavy-set worker seated beneath a pier, circular food tins stacked in a neat tower.
candidates.setup: Has finally found ten quiet minutes and has no affection for the broker.
candidates.quirk: Sets every bite on a clean tin lid before dealing with an interruption.
candidates.role: Sees Taffy slipping through with something valuable and makes a quiet choice to keep eating. A possible humane beat during the tension.

candidates.name: The Scrap Sweeper
candidates.silhouette: Wiry humanoid towing a low bundle of metal with a long magnetic collecting pole.
candidates.setup: Paid by recovered weight; hates useful fragments being trampled into the drain.
candidates.quirk: Taps each piece against the pole and listens before adding it.
candidates.role: The pole sweeps across Taffy's path; a metal click from the stolen device could expose him. Creates a small precise obstacle rather than another chase.
candidates.biologicalDirection: Short organic sensory filaments supplement the sweeper's listening and handling when locating and sorting metal scrap.

candidates.name: The Shift Marshal
candidates.silhouette: Tall straight-backed human, faded high collar, broad freight-signalling paddle.
candidates.setup: Wants the final scheduled load through before shift change.
candidates.quirk: Keeps counting freight movements while dealing with people.
candidates.role: Checks the door's authorization signal and allows the apparent maintenance traffic onward; the wanted broadcast then changes how they read the children.

candidates.name: The Pass Clerk
candidates.silhouette: Round-helmeted humanoid at a small window, flat permit boards stacked like roof tiles.
candidates.setup: Wants an impeccable handover so nobody can blame them for an access error.
candidates.quirk: Aligns every battered permit edge before putting it down.
candidates.role: Adds a human inspection after the key opens the electronic boundary. A raised pen or held stare creates uncertainty without demanding another stolen object.
candidates.biologicalDirection: A small near-focus eye pair can follow permits while the main eyes keep attention on arrivals.

candidates.name: The Relay Electrician
candidates.silhouette: Wiry older human, short utility cape, loops of spare cable over one arm.
candidates.setup: Trying to get a failing public display back into service and get paid.
candidates.quirk: Tests it with the same two-finger tap after every repair.
candidates.role: Can bring the screen back at exactly the wrong moment for the children: the successful repair reveals their wanted broadcast. Establish the repair before the reveal.
candidates.biologicalDirection: Specialized contact skin on the working fingers supports delicate circuit checks while tougher wrist skin protects repeated handling.

candidates.name: The Freight Counter
candidates.silhouette: Broad-limbed humanoid with a little tally paddle held against one forearm.
candidates.setup: Answers for every load moving through the hall; unexplained numbers mean unpaid work.
candidates.quirk: Marks a tally with a sharp tap against their boot.
candidates.role: Provides a readable flow of authorized movement to join or wait behind. Notices that the two small figures do not belong to the expected load.

candidates.name: The Hall Cleaner
candidates.silhouette: Stooped human behind an extremely wide broom and a narrow wheeled bucket.
candidates.setup: Needs one clean stretch of floor before the next freight movement ruins it.
candidates.quirk: Turns the bucket to face the direction of the next sweep.
candidates.role: Occupies the first convenient hiding place inside. Avoiding the fresh floor makes the children pause in the screen's sightline.

candidates.name: The Port Messenger
candidates.silhouette: Slender offworld humanoid, long calves, one upright rigid delivery tube.
candidates.setup: Needs to reach cargo dispatch before its next transfer departs.
candidates.quirk: Always chooses their next doorway before finishing the current one.
candidates.role: Their purposeful exit toward the cargo ramp plants the onward route to the port. When the alert appears, a stopped step and turned head raise the stakes.
candidates.biologicalDirection: Springy digitigrade lower legs and protective eye membranes make the courier's movement and wind exposure visibly specialized.
